body.claim: In the 1973 oil crisis, price controls are described as having made the US shortage worse.
body.why: The system capped the price of old oil but let newly discovered oil sell for more. As a result, old oil was withdrawn from the market, creating greater scarcity. Lines at gas stations were common, and the AAA reported that in the last week of February 1974, 20% of US stations had no fuel.

probes.question: In this account, what happened to old oil under the price cap?
options: It was withdrawn from the market, creating greater scarcity

probes.question: True or false: the AAA reported that in the last week of February 1974, 20% of American gasoline stations had no fuel.

image_brief.show: File:AFTER HOURS IN A GASOLINE LINE ... - NARA - 555459.jpg (public domain) shows a gasoline line at a pump during the crisis

claims.claim: Price controls are described as having made the US shortage worse
claims.quote: Price controls exacerbated the crisis in the US.
claims.note: Page states it flatly; the card's 'described as' hedge is conservative and fine.

claims.claim: The system capped the price of old oil but let newly discovered oil sell for more
claims.quote: The system limited the price of "old oil", that which had already been discovered

claims.claim: As a result old oil was withdrawn from the market, creating greater scarcity (probe p1)
claims.quote: As a result, old oil was withdrawn from the market, creating greater scarcity.

claims.claim: Lines at gas stations were common
claims.quote: In other states, lines at gasoline stations were common.
claims.note: Page says 'in other states' (those where odd-even/other rationing was used); card states it generally, a minor generalisation.

claims.claim: AAA reported that in the last week of February 1974, 20% of US stations had no fuel (probe p2)
claims.quote: The American Automobile Association reported that in the last week of February 1974, 20% of American gasoline stations had no fuel.
